## Observation (read-only, 2026-11-18 PST)
Two occurrences on 2026-11-16, both on `sarcastic-specified-kodiakbear` (times UTC):
- `verify_completion_start` returned job `1794871413492186335-b6a138…` at 23:23:33. Autodeploy cut `/mcp` over to a new container (8093) at 23:23:27 and retired `rebar-mcp-b4e0d01b6491-8092` with `docker stop --time 1260` (graceful drain). At 23:24:36, `gate_status` returned `status: failed, verdict: daemon-stopped`. The index file then ended `passed / PASS`, written 23:25:36 by the draining container's daemon.
- `review_plan_start` returned job `1794872550672894186-492f05…` at 23:42:30. Cutover to 8092 came at 23:44:25. At 23:49:37, `gate_status` returned `failed / daemon-stopped`. The index ended `passed / PASS` at 23:51:57.
The caller acted on the false failure and started a duplicate, billable run each time (23:24:45 and 23:49:58).

## Mechanism (from code)
`gate_runs._running_record_is_stale` treats a `running` index record as crashed whenever `_mcp_inflight.is_job_active(job_id)` is false. That registry lives in process memory. Both containers share the `.rebar/gate_runs` index on the `gerrit_mcp_code` volume, so the new container has no registry entry for the old container's job. `_materialize_stale_running` then writes `failed` into the shared index, and the old daemon overwrites it later. Autodeploy deliberately keeps the old container draining for up to 1,260 s, so this is the expected path for every gate that spans a cutover.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A regression test simulates a job whose `running` index record was written by another process that is still alive, and asserts `gate_status` does not report `failed` or overwrite the index while that owner is live.
- [ ] A job whose owning process really died is still materialized as failed (existing behaviour kept, test kept green).
compiled_state.title: After an MCP blue-green cutover, gate_status on the new container marks a job still running on the draining container as failed (daemon-stopped)
